newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate up to 14 pct from 11.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate up to 14 pct from 11.5 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate jumped to 14.0 percent on Friday from 11.5 percent, boosted by the volume of term loans at higher rates.
The daily trade totalled 26.5 million kuna, against 40 million on offer. However not all demand was met as lenders and borrowers could not agree on terms, dealers said.
Fresh borrowings accounted for 9.2 million, made at steady rates ranging from 11 percent for call money and 15 percent for two one-month loans.
Creditors also raised interest on previous call money loans to 11 from 9.0 percent.
Insurers charged 10 percent for old money. Rates for previous interbank loans ranged between 12 percent for short-term placements and 18 percent for one-month loans.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates at 5.6176 against the dollar and 3.5622 against the mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
